      "chunk": "Join us live: How we cut bloat in Storybook\n\n* Docs\n* Addons\n* Showcase\n* Blog\n* Visual Test\n* Enterprise\n\n87,213\n\nSearch docs\n\nDocs \n\nStorybook DocsDocs » Get Started » Frameworks » Next.js\n\nDocumentationAPITutorialsAddonsChangelog\n\nVersion 9.0\n* Get Started  \n   * Why Storybook?  \n   * Install  \n   * Frameworks  \n   * What's a story?  \n   * Browse stories  \n   * Setup  \n   * Conclusion\n* Stories  \n   * Args  \n   * Parameters  \n   * Decorators  \n   * Play function  \n   * Loaders  \n   * Tags  \n   * Naming components and hierarchy  \n   * Mocking data and modules  \n   * Building pages and screens  \n   * Stories for multiple components  \n   * Writing stories in TypeScript\n* Testing  \n   * Interaction tests  \n   * Accessibility tests  \n   * Visual tests  \n   * Snapshot tests  \n   * Test coverage  \n   * In CI  \n   * Integrations\n* Docs  \n   * Autodocs  \n   * MDX  \n   * Doc blocks  \n   * Code panel  \n   * Preview and build docs\n* Sharing  \n   * Publish  \n   * Embed  \n   * Design integrations  \n   * Composition  \n   * Package Composition\n* Essentials  \n   * Actions  \n   * Backgrounds  \n   * Controls  \n   * Highlight  \n   * Measure \u0026 outline  \n   * Toolbars \u0026 globals  \n   * Viewport\n* Addons  \n   * Install  \n   * Write  \n   * Configure addons  \n   * Write a preset  \n   * Add to catalog  \n   * Types of addons  \n   * Knowledge base  \n   * Addon API  \n   * Migrate addons to 9.0\n* Configure  \n   * Styling and CSS  \n   * Upgrading  \n   * Telemetry  \n   * Integration  \n   * Story rendering  \n   * Story layout  \n   * User Interface  \n   * Environment variables\n* Builders  \n   * Vite  \n   * Webpack  \n   * API\n* API  \n   * main.js|ts configuration  \n   * Component Story Format (CSF)  \n   * ArgTypes  \n   * Parameters  \n   * Doc Blocks  \n   * Portable Stories  \n   * Frameworks  \n   * CLI options\n* Contribute  \n   * RFC process  \n   * Code  \n   * Documentation  \n   * Frameworks  \n   * Reproduce  \n   * Roadmap\n* FAQ\n* Migrate to 9.0  \n   * Migrate from 7.x to 8.0\n\n# Storybook for Next.js\n\nStorybook for Next.js is a framework that makes it easy to develop and test UI components in isolation for Next.js applications. It includes:\n\n* 🔀 Routing\n* 🖼 Image optimization\n* ⤵️ Absolute imports\n* 🎨 Styling\n* 🎛 Webpack \u0026 Babel config\n* 💫 and more!\n\n## Requirements\n\n* Next.js ≥ 14.1\n\n## Getting started\n\n### In a project without Storybook\n\nFollow the prompts after running this command in your Next.js project's root directory:\n\nnpm\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpm create storybook@latest\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nMore on getting started with Storybook.\n\n### In a project with Storybook\n\nThis framework is designed to work with Storybook 7+. If you’re not already using v7, upgrade with this command:\n\nnpm\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpx storybook@latest upgrade\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Automatic migration\n\nWhen running the &#96;upgrade&#96; command above, you should get a prompt asking you to migrate to &#96;@storybook/nextjs&#96;, which should handle everything for you. In case that auto-migration does not work for your project, refer to the manual migration below.\n\n#### Manual migration\n\nFirst, install the framework:\n\nnpm\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpm install --save-dev @storybook/nextjs\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThen, update your &#96;.storybook/main.js|ts&#96; to change the framework property:\n\n.storybook/main.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport type { StorybookConfig } from '@storybook/nextjs';\n \nconst config: StorybookConfig = {\n  // ...\n  // framework: '@storybook/react-webpack5', 👈 Remove this\n  framework: '@storybook/nextjs', // 👈 Add this\n};\n \nexport default config;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nFinally, if you were using Storybook plugins to integrate with Next.js, those are no longer necessary when using this framework and can be removed:\n\n.storybook/main.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport type { StorybookConfig } from '@storybook/nextjs';\n \nconst config: StorybookConfig = {\n  // ...\n  addons: [\n    // ...\n    // 👇 These can both be removed\n    // 'storybook-addon-next',\n    // 'storybook-addon-next-router',\n  ],\n};\n \nexport default config;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### With Vite\n\nStorybook recommends using the &#96;@storybook/nextjs-vite&#96; framework, which is based on Vite and removes the need for Webpack and Babel. It supports all of the features documented here.\n\nnpm\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpm install --save-dev @storybook/nextjs-vite\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThen, update your &#96;.storybook/main.js|ts&#96; to change the framework property:\n\n.storybook/main.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport type { StorybookConfig } from '@storybook/nextjs-vite';\n \nconst config: StorybookConfig = {\n  // ...\n  // framework: '@storybook/react-webpack5', 👈 Remove this\n  framework: '@storybook/nextjs-vite', // 👈 Add this\n};\n \nexport default config;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nℹ️\n\nIf your Storybook configuration contains custom Webpack operations in webpackFinal, you will likely need to create equivalents in viteFinal.\n\nFor more information, see the Vite builder documentation.\n\nFinally, if you were using Storybook plugins to integrate with Next.js, those are no longer necessary when using this framework and can be removed:\n\n.storybook/main.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport type { StorybookConfig } from '@storybook/nextjs-vite';\n \nconst config: StorybookConfig = {\n  // ...\n  addons: [\n    // ...\n    // 👇 These can both be removed\n    // 'storybook-addon-next',\n    // 'storybook-addon-next-router',\n  ],\n};\n \nexport default config;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Run the Setup Wizard\n\nIf all goes well, you should see a setup wizard that will help you get started with Storybook introducing you to the main concepts and features, including how the UI is organized, how to write your first story, and how to test your components' response to various inputs utilizing controls.\n\nStorybook onboarding\n\nIf you skipped the wizard, you can always run it again by adding the &#96;?path=/onboarding&#96; query parameter to the URL of your Storybook instance, provided that the example stories are still available.\n\n## Next.js's Image component\n\nThis framework allows you to use Next.js's next/image with no configuration.\n\n### Local images\n\nLocal images are supported.\n\nindex.jsx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport Image from 'next/image';\nimport profilePic from '../public/me.png';\n \nfunction Home() {\n  return (\n    \u003c\u003e\n      \u003ch1\u003eMy Homepage\u003c/h1\u003e\n      \u003cImage\n        src={profilePic}\n        alt=\"Picture of the author\"\n        // width={500} automatically provided\n        // height={500} automatically provided\n        // blurDataURL=\"../public/me.png\" set to equal the image itself (for this framework)\n        // placeholder=\"blur\" // Optional blur-up while loading\n      /\u003e\n      \u003cp\u003eWelcome to my homepage!\u003c/p\u003e\n    \u003c/\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Remote images\n\nRemote images are also supported.\n\nindex.jsx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport Image from 'next/image';\n \nexport default function Home() {\n  return (\n    \u003c\u003e\n      \u003ch1\u003eMy Homepage\u003c/h1\u003e\n      \u003cImage src=\"/me.png\" alt=\"Picture of the author\" width={500} height={500} /\u003e\n      \u003cp\u003eWelcome to my homepage!\u003c/p\u003e\n    \u003c/\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Next.js font optimization\n\nnext/font is partially supported in Storybook. The packages &#96;next/font/google&#96; and &#96;next/font/local&#96; are supported.\n\n### next/font/google\n\nYou don't have to do anything. &#96;next/font/google&#96; is supported out of the box.\n\n### next/font/local\n\nFor local fonts you have to define the src property. The path is relative to the directory where the font loader function is called.\n\nIf the following component defines your localFont like this:\n\nsrc/components/MyComponent.js\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport localFont from 'next/font/local';\n \nconst localRubikStorm = localFont({ src: './fonts/RubikStorm-Regular.ttf' });\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### staticDir mapping\n\nℹ️\n\nYou can safely skip this section if you are using @storybook/nextjs-vite instead of &#96;@storybook/nextjs&#96;. The Vite-based framework takes care of the mapping automatically.\n\nYou have to tell Storybook where the &#96;fonts&#96; directory is located, via the staticDirs configuration. The &#96;from&#96; value is relative to the &#96;.storybook&#96; directory. The &#96;to&#96; value is relative to the execution context of Storybook. Very likely it is the root of your project.\n\n.storybook/main.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { StorybookConfig } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nconst config: StorybookConfig = {\n  // ...\n  staticDirs: [\n    {\n      from: '../src/components/fonts',\n      to: 'src/components/fonts',\n    },\n  ],\n};\n \nexport default config;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Not supported features of next/font\n\nThe following features are not supported (yet). Support for these features might be planned for the future:\n\n* Support font loaders configuration in next.config.js\n* fallback option\n* adjustFontFallback option\n* preload option gets ignored. Storybook handles Font loading its own way.\n* display option gets ignored. All fonts are loaded with display set to \"block\" to make Storybook load the font properly.\n\n### Mocking fonts during testing\n\nOccasionally fetching fonts from Google may fail as part of your Storybook build step. It is highly recommended to mock these requests, as those failures can cause your pipeline to fail as well. Next.js supports mocking fonts via a JavaScript module located where the env var &#96;NEXT_FONT_GOOGLE_MOCKED_RESPONSES&#96; references.\n\nFor example, using GitHub Actions:\n\n.github/workflows/ci.yml\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n- uses: chromaui/action@latest\n  env:\n    #👇 the location of mocked fonts to use\n    NEXT_FONT_GOOGLE_MOCKED_RESPONSES: ${{ github.workspace }}/mocked-google-fonts.js\n  with:\n    projectToken: ${{ secrets.CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN }}\n    token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYour mocked fonts will look something like this:\n\nmocked-google-fonts.js\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n//👇 Mocked responses of google fonts with the URL as the key\nmodule.exports = {\n  'https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;800\u0026display=block': &#96;\n    /* cyrillic-ext */\n    @font-face {\n      font-family: 'Inter';\n      font-style: normal;\n      font-weight: 400;\n      font-display: block;\n      src: url(https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/inter/v12/UcCO3FwrK3iLTeHuS_fvQtMwCp50KnMw2boKoduKmMEVuLyfAZJhiJ-Ek-_EeAmM.woff2) format('woff2');\n      unicode-range: U+0460-052F, U+1C80-1C88, U+20B4, U+2DE0-2DFF, U+A640-A69F, U+FE2E-FE2F;\n    }\n    /* more font declarations go here */\n    /* latin */\n    @font-face {\n      font-family: 'Inter';\n      font-style: normal;\n      font-weight: 400;\n      font-display: block;\n      src: url(https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/inter/v12/UcCO3FwrK3iLTeHuS_fvQtMwCp50KnMw2boKoduKmMEVuLyfAZ9hiJ-Ek-_EeA.woff2) format('woff2');\n      unicode-range: U+0000-00FF, U+0131, U+0152-0153, U+02BB-02BC, U+02C6, U+02DA, U+02DC, U+0304, U+0308, U+0329, U+2000-206F, U+2074, U+20AC, U+2122, U+2191, U+2193, U+2212, U+2215, U+FEFF, U+FFFD;\n    }&#96;,\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Next.js routing\n\nNext.js's router is automatically stubbed for you so that when the router is interacted with, all of its interactions are automatically logged to the Actions panel if you have the Storybook actions addon.\n\nYou should only use &#96;next/router&#96; in the &#96;pages&#96; directory. In the &#96;app&#96; directory, it is necessary to use &#96;next/navigation&#96;.\n\n### Overriding defaults\n\nPer-story overrides can be done by adding a &#96;nextjs.router&#96; property onto the story parameters. The framework will shallowly merge whatever you put here into the router.\n\nRouterBasedComponent.stories.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport RouterBasedComponent from './RouterBasedComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: RouterBasedComponent,\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof RouterBasedComponent\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\ntype Story = StoryObj\u003ctypeof meta\u003e;\n \n// If you have the actions addon,\n// you can interact with the links and see the route change events there\nexport const Example: Story = {\n  parameters: {\n    nextjs: {\n      router: {\n        pathname: '/profile/[id]',\n        asPath: '/profile/1',\n        query: {\n          id: '1',\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThese overrides can also be applied to all stories for a component or all stories in your project. Standard parameter inheritance rules apply.\n\n### Default router\n\nThe default values on the stubbed router are as follows (see globals for more details on how globals work).\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Default router\nconst defaultRouter = {\n  // The locale should be configured globally: https://storybook.js.org/docs/essentials/toolbars-and-globals#globals\n  locale: globals?.locale,\n  asPath: '/',\n  basePath: '/',\n  isFallback: false,\n  isLocaleDomain: false,\n  isReady: true,\n  isPreview: false,\n  route: '/',\n  pathname: '/',\n  query: {},\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAdditionally, the router object contains all of the original methods (such as &#96;push()&#96;, &#96;replace()&#96;, etc.) as mock functions that can be manipulated and asserted on using regular mock APIs.\n\nTo override these defaults, you can use parameters and beforeEach:\n\n.storybook/preview.js|ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Preview } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \n// 👇 Must include the &#96;.mock&#96; portion of filename to have mocks typed correctly\nimport { getRouter } from \"@storybook/your-framework/router.mock\";\n \nconst preview: Preview = {\n  parameters: {\n    nextjs: {\n      // 👇 Override the default router properties\n      router: {\n        basePath: '/app/',\n      },\n    },\n  },\n  async beforeEach() {\n    // 👇 Manipulate the default router method mocks\n    getRouter().push.mockImplementation(() =\u003e {\n      /* ... */\n    });\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Next.js navigation\n\nPlease note that next/navigation can only be used in components/pages in the &#96;app&#96; directory.\n\n### Set nextjs.appDirectory to true\n\nIf your story imports components that use &#96;next/navigation&#96;, you need to set the parameter &#96;nextjs.appDirectory&#96; to &#96;true&#96; in for that component's stories:\n\nNavigationBasedComponent.stories.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport NavigationBasedComponent from './NavigationBasedComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: NavigationBasedComponent,\n  parameters: {\n    nextjs: {\n      appDirectory: true, // 👈 Set this\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof NavigationBasedComponent\u003e;\nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIf your Next.js project uses the &#96;app&#96; directory for every page (in other words, it does not have a &#96;pages&#96; directory), you can set the parameter &#96;nextjs.appDirectory&#96; to &#96;true&#96; in the .storybook/preview.js|ts file to apply it to all stories.\n\n.storybook/preview.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Preview } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nconst preview: Preview = {\n  // ...\n  parameters: {\n    // ...\n    nextjs: {\n      appDirectory: true,\n    },\n  },\n};\n \nexport default preview;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Overriding defaults\n\nPer-story overrides can be done by adding a &#96;nextjs.navigation&#96; property onto the story parameters. The framework will shallowly merge whatever you put here into the router.\n\nNavigationBasedComponent.stories.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport NavigationBasedComponent from './NavigationBasedComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: NavigationBasedComponent,\n  parameters: {\n    nextjs: {\n      appDirectory: true,\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof NavigationBasedComponent\u003e;\nexport default meta;\n \ntype Story = StoryObj\u003ctypeof meta\u003e;\n \n// If you have the actions addon,\n// you can interact with the links and see the route change events there\nexport const Example: Story = {\n  parameters: {\n    nextjs: {\n      navigation: {\n        pathname: '/profile',\n        query: {\n          user: '1',\n        },\n      },\n    },\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThese overrides can also be applied to all stories for a component or all stories in your project. Standard parameter inheritance rules apply.\n\n### useSelectedLayoutSegment, useSelectedLayoutSegments, and useParams hooks\n\nThe &#96;useSelectedLayoutSegment&#96;, &#96;useSelectedLayoutSegments&#96;, and &#96;useParams&#96; hooks are supported in Storybook. You have to set the &#96;nextjs.navigation.segments&#96; parameter to return the segments or the params you want to use.\n\nNavigationBasedComponent.stories.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport NavigationBasedComponent from './NavigationBasedComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: NavigationBasedComponent,\n  parameters: {\n    nextjs: {\n      appDirectory: true,\n      navigation: {\n        segments: ['dashboard', 'analytics'],\n      },\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof NavigationBasedComponent\u003e;\nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nWith the above configuration, the component rendered in the stories would receive the following values from the hooks:\n\nNavigationBasedComponent.js\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport { useSelectedLayoutSegment, useSelectedLayoutSegments, useParams } from 'next/navigation';\n \nexport default function NavigationBasedComponent() {\n  const segment = useSelectedLayoutSegment(); // dashboard\n  const segments = useSelectedLayoutSegments(); // [\"dashboard\", \"analytics\"]\n  const params = useParams(); // {}\n  // ...\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nTo use &#96;useParams&#96;, you have to use a segments array where each element is an array containing two strings. The first string is the param key and the second string is the param value.\n\nNavigationBasedComponent.stories.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport NavigationBasedComponent from './NavigationBasedComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: NavigationBasedComponent,\n  parameters: {\n    nextjs: {\n      appDirectory: true,\n      navigation: {\n        segments: [\n          ['slug', 'hello'],\n          ['framework', 'nextjs'],\n        ],\n      },\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof NavigationBasedComponent\u003e;\nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nWith the above configuration, the component rendered in the stories would receive the following values from the hooks:\n\nParamsBasedComponent.js\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport { useSelectedLayoutSegment, useSelectedLayoutSegments, useParams } from 'next/navigation';\n \nexport default function ParamsBasedComponent() {\n  const segment = useSelectedLayoutSegment(); // hello\n  const segments = useSelectedLayoutSegments(); // [\"hello\", \"nextjs\"]\n  const params = useParams(); // { slug: \"hello\", framework: \"nextjs\" }\n  ...\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThese overrides can also be applied to a single story or all stories in your project. Standard parameter inheritance rules apply.\n\nThe default value of &#96;nextjs.navigation.segments&#96; is &#96;[]&#96; if not set.\n\n### Default navigation context\n\nThe default values on the stubbed navigation context are as follows:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Default navigation context\nconst defaultNavigationContext = {\n  pathname: '/',\n  query: {},\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAdditionally, the router object contains all of the original methods (such as &#96;push()&#96;, &#96;replace()&#96;, etc.) as mock functions that can be manipulated and asserted on using regular mock APIs.\n\nTo override these defaults, you can use parameters and beforeEach:\n\n.storybook/preview.js|ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Preview } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \n// 👇 Must include the &#96;.mock&#96; portion of filename to have mocks typed correctly\nimport { getRouter } from '@storybook/your-framework/navigation.mock';\n \nconst preview: Preview = {\n  parameters: {\n    nextjs: {\n      // 👇 Override the default navigation properties\n      navigation: {\n        pathname: '/app/',\n      },\n    },\n  },\n  async beforeEach() {\n    // 👇 Manipulate the default navigation method mocks\n    getRouter().push.mockImplementation(() =\u003e {\n      /* ... */\n    });\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Next.js Head\n\nnext/head is supported out of the box. You can use it in your stories like you would in your Next.js application. Please keep in mind, that the Head &#96;children&#96; are placed into the head element of the iframe that Storybook uses to render your stories.\n\n## Sass/Scss\n\nGlobal Sass/Scss stylesheets are supported without any additional configuration as well. Just import them into .storybook/preview.js|ts\n\n.storybook/preview.js|ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport '../styles/globals.scss';\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will automatically include any of your custom Sass configurations in your &#96;next.config.js&#96; file.\n\nnext.config.js\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport * as path from 'path';\n \nexport default {\n  // Any options here are included in Sass compilation for your stories\n  sassOptions: {\n    includePaths: [path.join(__dirname, 'styles')],\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## CSS/Sass/Scss Modules\n\nCSS modules work as expected.\n\nsrc/components/Button.jsx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// This import will work in Storybook\nimport styles from './Button.module.css';\n// Sass/Scss is also supported\n// import styles from './Button.module.scss'\n// import styles from './Button.module.sass'\n \nexport function Button() {\n  return (\n    \u003cbutton type=\"button\" className={styles.error}\u003e\n      Destroy\n    \u003c/button\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Styled JSX\n\nThe built in CSS-in-JS solution for Next.js is styled-jsx, and this framework supports that out of the box too, zero config.\n\nsrc/components/HelloWorld.jsx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// This will work in Storybook\nfunction HelloWorld() {\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv\u003e\n      Hello world\n      \u003cp\u003escoped!\u003c/p\u003e\n      \u003cstyle jsx\u003e{&#96;\n        p {\n          color: blue;\n        }\n        div {\n          background: red;\n        }\n        @media (max-width: 600px) {\n          div {\n            background: blue;\n          }\n        }\n      &#96;}\u003c/style\u003e\n      \u003cstyle global jsx\u003e{&#96;\n        body {\n          background: black;\n        }\n      &#96;}\u003c/style\u003e\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  );\n}\n \nexport default HelloWorld;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can use your own babel config too. This is an example of how you can customize styled-jsx.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// .babelrc (or whatever config file you use)\n{\n  \"presets\": [\n    [\n      \"next/babel\",\n      {\n        \"styled-jsx\": {\n          \"plugins\": [\"@styled-jsx/plugin-sass\"]\n        }\n      }\n    ]\n  ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## PostCSS\n\nNext.js lets you customize PostCSS config. Thus this framework will automatically handle your PostCSS config for you.\n\nThis allows for cool things like zero-config Tailwind! (See Next.js' example)\n\n## Absolute imports\n\nAbsolute imports from the root directory are supported.\n\nindex.jsx|tsx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// All good!\nimport Button from 'components/button';\n// Also good!\nimport styles from 'styles/HomePage.module.css';\n \nexport default function HomePage() {\n  return (\n    \u003c\u003e\n      \u003ch1 className={styles.title}\u003eHello World\u003c/h1\u003e\n      \u003cButton /\u003e\n    \u003c/\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAlso OK for global styles in &#96;.storybook/preview.js|ts&#96;!\n\n.storybook/preview.js|ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport 'styles/globals.scss';\n \n// ...\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n⚠️\n\nAbsolute imports **cannot** be mocked in stories/tests. See the Mocking modules section for more information.\n\n## Module aliases\n\nModule aliases are also supported.\n\nindex.jsx|tsx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// All good!\nimport Button from '@/components/button';\n// Also good!\nimport styles from '@/styles/HomePage.module.css';\n \nexport default function HomePage() {\n  return (\n    \u003c\u003e\n      \u003ch1 className={styles.title}\u003eHello World\u003c/h1\u003e\n      \u003cButton /\u003e\n    \u003c/\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Subpath imports\n\nAs an alternative to module aliases, you can use subpath imports to import modules. This follows Node package standards and has benefits when mocking modules.\n\nTo configure subpath imports, you define the &#96;imports&#96; property in your project's &#96;package.json&#96; file. This property maps the subpath to the actual file path. The example below configures subpath imports for all modules in the project:\n\npackage.json\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  \"imports\": {\n    \"#*\": [\"./*\", \"./*.ts\", \"./*.tsx\"]\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nℹ️\n\nBecause subpath imports replace module aliases, you can remove the path aliases from your TypeScript configuration.\n\nWhich can then be used like this:\n\nindex.jsx|tsx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport Button from '#components/button';\nimport styles from '#styles/HomePage.module.css';\n \nexport default function HomePage() {\n  return (\n    \u003c\u003e\n      \u003ch1 className={styles.title}\u003eHello World\u003c/h1\u003e\n      \u003cButton /\u003e\n    \u003c/\u003e\n  );\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Mocking modules\n\nComponents often depend on modules that are imported into the component file. These can be from external packages or internal to your project. When rendering those components in Storybook or testing them, you may want to mock those modules to control and assert their behavior.\n\n### Built-in mocked modules\n\nThis framework provides mocks for many of Next.js' internal modules:\n\n1. @storybook/nextjs/cache.mock\n2. @storybook/nextjs/headers.mock\n3. @storybook/nextjs/navigation.mock\n4. @storybook/nextjs/router.mock\n\n### Mocking other modules\n\nHow you mock other modules in Storybook depends on how you import the module into your component.\n\nWith either approach, the first step is to create a mock file. Here's an example of a mock file for a module named &#96;session&#96;:\n\nlib/session.mock.ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport { fn } from 'storybook/test';\nimport * as actual from './session';\n \nexport * from './session';\nexport const getUserFromSession = fn(actual.getUserFromSession).mockName('getUserFromSession');\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### With subpath imports\n\nIf you're using subpath imports, you can adjust your configuration to apply conditions so that the mocked module is used inside Storybook. The example below configures subpath imports for four internal modules, which are then mocked in Storybook:\n\npackage.json\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  \"imports\": {\n    \"#api\": {\n      // storybook condition applies to Storybook\n      \"storybook\": \"./api.mock.ts\",\n      \"default\": \"./api.ts\",\n    },\n    \"#app/actions\": {\n      \"storybook\": \"./app/actions.mock.ts\",\n      \"default\": \"./app/actions.ts\",\n    },\n    \"#lib/session\": {\n      \"storybook\": \"./lib/session.mock.ts\",\n      \"default\": \"./lib/session.ts\",\n    },\n    \"#lib/db\": {\n      // test condition applies to test environments *and* Storybook\n      \"test\": \"./lib/db.mock.ts\",\n      \"default\": \"./lib/db.ts\",\n    },\n    \"#*\": [\"./*\", \"./*.ts\", \"./*.tsx\"],\n  },\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nℹ️\n\nEach subpath must begin with &#96;#&#96;, to differentiate it from a regular module path. The &#96;#*&#96; entry is a catch-all that maps all subpaths to the root directory.\n\n#### With module aliases\n\nIf you're using module aliases, you can add a Webpack alias to your Storybook configuration to point to the mock file.\n\nvitewebpack\n\n.storybook/main.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with the framework you are using, e.g. react-vite, nextjs-vite, vue3-vite, etc.\nimport type { StorybookConfig } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nconst config: StorybookConfig = {\n  framework: '@storybook/your-framework',\n  stories: ['../src/**/*.mdx', '../src/**/*.stories.@(js|jsx|mjs|ts|tsx)'],\n  viteFinal: async (config) =\u003e {\n    if (config.resolve) {\n      config.resolve.alias = {\n        ...config.resolve?.alias,\n        // 👇 External module\n        lodash: require.resolve('./lodash.mock'),\n        // 👇 Internal modules\n        '@/api': path.resolve(__dirname, './api.mock.ts'),\n        '@/app/actions': path.resolve(__dirname, './app/actions.mock.ts'),\n        '@/lib/session': path.resolve(__dirname, './lib/session.mock.ts'),\n        '@/lib/db': path.resolve(__dirname, './lib/db.mock.ts'),\n      };\n    }\n \n    return config;\n  },\n};\n \nexport default config;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Runtime config\n\nNext.js allows for Runtime Configuration which lets you import a handy &#96;getConfig&#96; function to get certain configuration defined in your &#96;next.config.js&#96; file at runtime.\n\nIn the context of Storybook with this framework, you can expect Next.js's Runtime Configuration feature to work just fine.\n\nNote, because Storybook doesn't server render your components, your components will only see what they normally see on the client side (i.e. they won't see &#96;serverRuntimeConfig&#96; but will see &#96;publicRuntimeConfig&#96;).\n\nFor example, consider the following Next.js config:\n\nnext.config.js\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nmodule.exports = {\n  serverRuntimeConfig: {\n    mySecret: 'secret',\n    secondSecret: process.env.SECOND_SECRET, // Pass through env variables\n  },\n  publicRuntimeConfig: {\n    staticFolder: '/static',\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCalls to &#96;getConfig&#96; would return the following object when called within Storybook:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Runtime config\n{\n  \"serverRuntimeConfig\": {},\n  \"publicRuntimeConfig\": {\n    \"staticFolder\": \"/static\"\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Custom Webpack config\n\nℹ️\n\nYou can safely skip this section if you are using &#96;@storybook/nextjs-vite&#96; instead of &#96;@storybook/nextjs&#96;. The Vite-based Next.js framework does not support Webpack settings.\n\nNext.js comes with a lot of things for free out of the box like Sass support, but sometimes you add custom Webpack config modifications to Next.js. This framework takes care of most of the Webpack modifications you would want to add. If Next.js supports a feature out of the box, then that feature will work out of the box in Storybook. If Next.js doesn't support something out of the box, but makes it easy to configure, then this framework will do the same for that thing for Storybook.\n\nAny Webpack modifications desired for Storybook should be made in .storybook/main.js|ts.\n\nNote: Not all Webpack modifications are copy/paste-able between &#96;next.config.js&#96; and &#96;.storybook/main.js|ts&#96;. It is recommended to do your research on how to properly make your modification to Storybook's Webpack config and on how Webpack works.\n\nBelow is an example of how to add SVGR support to Storybook with this framework.\n\n.storybook/main.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport type { StorybookConfig } from '@storybook/nextjs';\n \nconst config: StorybookConfig = {\n  // ...\n  webpackFinal: async (config) =\u003e {\n    config.module = config.module || {};\n    config.module.rules = config.module.rules || [];\n \n    // This modifies the existing image rule to exclude .svg files\n    // since you want to handle those files with @svgr/webpack\n    const imageRule = config.module.rules.find((rule) =\u003e rule?.['test']?.test('.svg'));\n    if (imageRule) {\n      imageRule['exclude'] = /\\.svg$/;\n    }\n \n    // Configure .svg files to be loaded with @svgr/webpack\n    config.module.rules.push({\n      test: /\\.svg$/,\n      use: ['@svgr/webpack'],\n    });\n \n    return config;\n  },\n};\n \nexport default config;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Typescript\n\nStorybook handles most Typescript configurations, but this framework adds additional support for Next.js's support for Absolute Imports and Module path aliases. In short, it takes into account your &#96;tsconfig.json&#96;'s baseUrl and paths. Thus, a &#96;tsconfig.json&#96; like the one below would work out of the box.\n\ntsconfig.json\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  \"compilerOptions\": {\n    \"baseUrl\": \".\",\n    \"paths\": {\n      \"@/components/*\": [\"components/*\"]\n    }\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## React Server Components (RSC)\n\n(⚠️ **Experimental**)\n\nIf your app uses React Server Components (RSC), Storybook can render them in stories in the browser.\n\nTo enable this set the &#96;experimentalRSC&#96; feature flag in your &#96;.storybook/main.js|ts&#96; config:\n\n.storybook/main.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { StorybookConfig } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nconst config: StorybookConfig = {\n  // ...\n  features: {\n    experimentalRSC: true,\n  },\n};\n \nexport default config;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nSetting this flag automatically wraps your story in a Suspense wrapper, which is able to render asynchronous components in NextJS's version of React.\n\nIf this wrapper causes problems in any of your existing stories, you can selectively disable it using the &#96;react.rsc&#96; parameter at the global/component/story level:\n\nMyServerComponent.stories.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport MyServerComponent from './MyServerComponent';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: MyServerComponent,\n  parameters: {\n    react: { rsc: false },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof MyServerComponent\u003e;\nexport default meta;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNote that wrapping your server components in Suspense does not help if your server components access server-side resources like the file system or Node-specific libraries. To work around this, you'll need to mock out your data access layer using Webpack aliases or an addon like storybook-addon-module-mock.\n\nIf your server components access data via the network, we recommend using the MSW Storybook Addon to mock network requests.\n\nIn the future we will provide better mocking support in Storybook and support for Server Actions.\n\n## Notes for Yarn v2 and v3 users\n\nIf you're using Yarn v2 or v3, you may run into issues where Storybook can't resolve &#96;style-loader&#96; or &#96;css-loader&#96;. For example, you might get errors like:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nModule not found: Error: Can't resolve 'css-loader'\nModule not found: Error: Can't resolve 'style-loader'\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis is because those versions of Yarn have different package resolution rules than Yarn v1.x. If this is the case for you, please install the package directly.\n\n## FAQ\n\n### Stories for pages/components which fetch data\n\nNext.js pages can fetch data directly within server components in the &#96;app&#96; directory, which often include module imports that only run in a node environment. This does not (currently) work within Storybook, because if you import from a Next.js page file containing those node module imports in your stories, your Storybook's Webpack will crash because those modules will not run in a browser. To get around this, you can extract the component in your page file into a separate file and import that pure component in your stories. Or, if that's not feasible for some reason, you can polyfill those modules in your Storybook's webpackFinal configuration.\n\n**Before**\n\napp/my-page/index.jsx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nasync function getData() {\n  const res = await fetch(...);\n  // ...\n}\n \n// Using this component in your stories will break the Storybook build\nexport default async function Page() {\n  const data = await getData();\n \n  return // ...\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**After**\n\napp/my-page/index.jsx\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Use this component in your stories\nimport MyPage from './components/MyPage';\n \nasync function getData() {\n  const res = await fetch(...);\n  // ...\n}\n \nexport default async function Page() {\n  const data = await getData();\n \n  return \u003cMyPage {...data} /\u003e;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Statically imported images won't load\n\nMake sure you are treating image imports the same way you treat them when using &#96;next/image&#96; in normal development.\n\nBefore using this framework, image imports would import the raw path to the image (e.g. &#96;'static/media/stories/assets/logo.svg'&#96;). Now image imports work the \"Next.js way\", meaning that you now get an object when importing an image. For example:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Image import object\n{\n  \"src\": \"static/media/stories/assets/logo.svg\",\n  \"height\": 48,\n  \"width\": 48,\n  \"blurDataURL\": \"static/media/stories/assets/logo.svg\"\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nTherefore, if something in Storybook isn't showing the image properly, make sure you expect the object to be returned from an import instead of only the asset path.\n\nSee local images for more detail on how Next.js treats static image imports.\n\n### Module not found: Error: Can't resolve package name\n\nYou might get this if you're using Yarn v2 or v3\\. See Notes for Yarn v2 and v3 users for more details.\n\n### What if I'm using the Vite builder?\n\nStorybook provides a Vite-based framework for Next.js. Follow the installation instructions and replace all instances of &#96;@storybook/nextjs&#96; with &#96;@storybook/nextjs-vite&#96;.\n\n### Error: You are importing avif images, but you don't have sharp installed. You have to install sharp in order to use image optimization features in Next.js.\n\n&#96;sharp&#96; is a dependency of Next.js's image optimization feature. If you see this error, you need to install &#96;sharp&#96; in your project.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpm install sharp\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nyarn add sharp\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\npnpm add sharp\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can refer to the Install sharp to Use Built-In Image Optimization in the Next.js documentation for more information.\n\n## API\n\n### Modules\n\nThe &#96;@storybook/nextjs&#96; package exports several modules that enable you to mock Next.js's internal behavior.\n\n#### @storybook/nextjs/export-mocks\n\nType: &#96;{ getPackageAliases: ({ useESM?: boolean }) =\u003e void }&#96;\n\n&#96;getPackageAliases&#96; is a helper for generating the aliases needed to set up portable stories.\n\njest.config.ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport type { Config } from 'jest';\nimport nextJest from 'next/jest.js';\n// 👇 Import the utility function\nimport { getPackageAliases } from '@storybook/nextjs/export-mocks';\n \nconst createJestConfig = nextJest({\n  // Provide the path to your Next.js app to load next.config.js and .env files in your test environment\n  dir: './',\n});\n \nconst config: Config = {\n  testEnvironment: 'jsdom',\n  // ... rest of Jest config\n  moduleNameMapper: {\n    ...getPackageAliases(), // 👈 Add the utility as mapped module names\n  },\n};\n \nexport default createJestConfig(config);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### @storybook/nextjs/cache.mock\n\nType: &#96;typeof import('next/cache')&#96;\n\nThis module exports mocked implementations of the &#96;next/cache&#96; module's exports. You can use it to create your own mock implementations or assert on mock calls in a story's play function.\n\nMyForm.stories.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { expect } from 'storybook/test';\n \n// 👇 Must include the &#96;.mock&#96; portion of filename to have mocks typed correctly\nimport { revalidatePath } from '@storybook/your-framework/cache.mock';\n \nimport MyForm from './my-form';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: MyForm,\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof MyForm\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\ntype Story = StoryObj\u003ctypeof meta\u003e;\n \nexport const Submitted: Story = {\n  async play({ canvas, userEvent }) {\n    const submitButton = canvas.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i });\n    await userEvent.click(saveButton);\n    // 👇 Use any mock assertions on the function\n    await expect(revalidatePath).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/');\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### @storybook/nextjs/headers.mock\n\nType: cookies, headers and draftMode from Next.js\n\nThis module exports _writable_ mocked implementations of the &#96;next/headers&#96; module's exports. You can use it to set up cookies or headers that are read in your story, and to later assert that they have been called.\n\nNext.js's default headers() export is read-only, but this module exposes methods allowing you to write to the headers:\n\n* **&#96;headers().append(name: string, value: string)&#96;**: Appends the value to the header if it exists already.\n* **&#96;headers().delete(name: string)&#96;**: Deletes the header\n* **&#96;headers().set(name: string, value: string)&#96;**: Sets the header to the value provided.\n\nFor cookies, you can use the existing API to write them. E.g., &#96;cookies().set('firstName', 'Jane')&#96;.\n\nBecause &#96;headers()&#96;, &#96;cookies()&#96; and their sub-functions are all mocks you can use any mock utilities in your stories, like &#96;headers().getAll.mock.calls&#96;.\n\nMyForm.stories.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { expect } from 'storybook/test';\n \n// 👇 Must include the &#96;.mock&#96; portion of filename to have mocks typed correctly\nimport { cookies, headers } from '@storybook/your-framework/headers.mock';\n \nimport MyForm from './my-form';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: MyForm,\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof MyForm\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\ntype Story = StoryObj\u003ctypeof meta\u003e;\n \nexport const LoggedInEurope: Story = {\n  async beforeEach() {\n    // 👇 Set mock cookies and headers ahead of rendering\n    cookies().set('username', 'Sol');\n    headers().set('timezone', 'Central European Summer Time');\n  },\n  async play() {\n    // 👇 Assert that your component called the mocks\n    await expect(cookies().get).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();\n    await expect(cookies().get).toHaveBeenCalledWith('username');\n    await expect(headers().get).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();\n    await expect(cookies().get).toHaveBeenCalledWith('timezone');\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### @storybook/nextjs/navigation.mock\n\nType: &#96;typeof import('next/navigation') \u0026 getRouter: () =\u003e ReturnType\u003ctypeof import('next/navigation')['useRouter']\u003e&#96;\n\nThis module exports mocked implementations of the &#96;next/navigation&#96; module's exports. It also exports a &#96;getRouter&#96; function that returns a mocked version of Next.js's router object from useRouter, allowing the properties to be manipulated and asserted on. You can use it mock implementations or assert on mock calls in a story's play function.\n\nMyForm.stories.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { expect } from 'storybook/test';\n \n// 👇 Must include the &#96;.mock&#96; portion of filename to have mocks typed correctly\nimport { redirect, getRouter } from '@storybook/your-framework/navigation.mock';\n \nimport MyForm from './my-form';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: MyForm,\n  parameters: {\n    nextjs: {\n      // 👇 As in the Next.js application, next/navigation only works using App Router\n      appDirectory: true,\n    },\n  },\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof MyForm\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\ntype Story = StoryObj\u003ctypeof meta\u003e;\n \nexport const Unauthenticated: Story = {\n  async play() {\n    // 👇 Assert that your component called redirect()\n    await expect(redirect).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/login', 'replace');\n  },\n};\n \nexport const GoBack: Story = {\n  async play({ canvas, userEvent }) {\n    const backBtn = await canvas.findByText('Go back');\n \n    await userEvent.click(backBtn);\n    // 👇 Assert that your component called back()\n    await expect(getRouter().back).toHaveBeenCalled();\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### @storybook/nextjs/router.mock\n\nType: &#96;typeof import('next/router') \u0026 getRouter: () =\u003e ReturnType\u003ctypeof import('next/router')['useRouter']\u003e&#96;\n\nThis module exports mocked implementations of the &#96;next/router&#96; module's exports. It also exports a &#96;getRouter&#96; function that returns a mocked version of Next.js's router object from useRouter, allowing the properties to be manipulated and asserted on. You can use it mock implementations or assert on mock calls in a story's play function.\n\nMyForm.stories.ts\n\nTypescript\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nimport type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/your-framework';\n \nimport { expect } from 'storybook/test';\n \n// 👇 Must include the &#96;.mock&#96; portion of filename to have mocks typed correctly\nimport { getRouter } from '@storybook/your-framework/router.mock';\n \nimport MyForm from './my-form';\n \nconst meta = {\n  component: MyForm,\n} satisfies Meta\u003ctypeof MyForm\u003e;\n \nexport default meta;\ntype Story = StoryObj\u003ctypeof meta\u003e;\n \nexport const GoBack: Story = {\n  async play({ canvas, userEvent }) {\n    const backBtn = await canvas.findByText('Go back');\n \n    await userEvent.click(backBtn);\n    // 👇 Assert that your component called back()\n    await expect(getRouter().back).toHaveBeenCalled();\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Options\n\nYou can pass an options object for additional configuration if needed:\n\n.storybook/main.js\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport * as path from 'path';\n \n// Replace your-framework with nextjs or nextjs-vite\nexport default {\n  // ...\n  framework: {\n    name: '@storybook/your-framework',\n    options: {\n      image: {\n        loading: 'eager',\n      },\n      nextConfigPath: path.resolve(__dirname, '../next.config.js'),\n    },\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe available options are:\n\n#### builder\n\nType: &#96;Record\u003cstring, any\u003e&#96;\n\nConfigure options for the framework's builder. For Next.js, available options can be found in the Webpack builder docs.\n\n#### image\n\nType: &#96;object&#96;\n\nProps to pass to every instance of &#96;next/image&#96;. See next/image docs for more details.\n\n#### nextConfigPath\n\nType: &#96;string&#96;\n\nThe absolute path to the &#96;next.config.js&#96; file. This is necessary if you have a custom &#96;next.config.js&#96; file that is not in the root directory of your project.\n\n### Parameters\n\nThis framework contributes the following parameters to Storybook, under the &#96;nextjs&#96; namespace:\n\n#### appDirectory\n\nType: &#96;boolean&#96;\n\nDefault: &#96;false&#96;\n\nIf your story imports components that use &#96;next/navigation&#96;, you need to set the parameter &#96;nextjs.appDirectory&#96; to &#96;true&#96;. Because this is a parameter, you can apply it to a single story, all stories for a component, or every story in your Storybook. See Next.js Navigation for more details.\n\n#### navigation\n\nType:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  asPath?: string;\n  pathname?: string;\n  query?: Record\u003cstring, string\u003e;\n  segments?: (string | [string, string])[];\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nDefault value:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  segments: [];\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe router object that is passed to the &#96;next/navigation&#96; context. See Next.js's navigation docs for more details.\n\n#### router\n\nType:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  asPath?: string;\n  pathname?: string;\n  query?: Record\u003cstring, string\u003e;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe router object that is passed to the &#96;next/router&#96; context. See Next.js's router docs for more details.\n\nWas this page useful?\n\n👍👎\n\n✍️ Edit on Github\n\nOn this page\n\nJoin the community\n\nSubscribe\n\n7,044 developers and counting\n\nWhy\n\nWhy StorybookComponent driven UI\n\nDocs\n\nGuidesTutorialsChangelogTelemetry\n\nCommunity\n\nAddonsGet involvedBlog\n\nShowcase\n\nExploreProjectsComponent glossary\n\nOpen source software\n\nMaintained by\n\nChromatic\n\nSpecial thanks to Netlify and CircleCI",
      "title": "Storybook for Next.js | Storybook docs",
      "url": "https://storybook.js.org/docs/get-started/frameworks/nextjs"
    },
    {
      "chunk": "Join us live: How we cut bloat in Storybook\n\n* Docs\n* Addons\n* Showcase\n* Blog\n* Visual Test\n* Enterprise\n\n87,213\n\nSearch docs\n\nBack to integrations\n\nnext\n\n# Integrate Next.js with Storybook\n\nNext.js enables you to create full-stack web applications by extending the latest React features\n\nℹ️\n\nPrerequisites\n\nThis recipe assumes that you have a Next \u003e= 12 app. Don’t have this? Follow Next's setup instructions then run:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n# Add Storybook:\nnpm create storybook@latest\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Set up your project\n\n### In a project without Storybook\n\nFollow the prompts after running this command in your Next.js project's root directory:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpm create storybook@latest\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### In a project with Storybook\n\nThis framework is designed to work with Storybook 7\\. If you’re not already using v7, upgrade with this command:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nnpx storybook@latest upgrade\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Automatic migration\n\nWhen running the upgrade command above, you should get a prompt asking you to migrate to &#96;@storybook/nextjs&#96;, which should handle everything for you. In case that auto-migration does not work for your project, refer to the manual migration below.\n\n#### Manual migration\n\nInstall the framework:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nyarn add -D @storybook/nextjs\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nUpdate your &#96;main.js&#96; to change the framework property:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// .storybook/main.js\n \nexport default {\n  // ...\n  framework: {\n    // name: '@storybook/react-webpack5', // Remove this\n    name: '@storybook/nextjs', // Add this\n    options: {},\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIf you were using Storybook plugins to integrate with Next.js, those are no longer necessary when using this framework and can be removed:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// .storybook/main.js\n \nexport default {\n  // ...\n  addons: [\n    // ...\n    // These can both be removed\n    // 'storybook-addon-next',\n    // 'storybook-addon-next-router',\n  ],\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### (Experimental) SWC support\n\nIf you're working with a Next.js project that already uses SWC (e.g., version 14 or higher), you can enable it in Storybook by adding the following to your &#96;main.js&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// .storybook/main.js\n \nexport default {\n  // ...\n  framework: {\n    name: '@storybook/nextjs',\n    options: {\n      builder: {\n        useSWC: true, // Enables SWC support\n      },\n    },\n  },\n};\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n💡\n\nSWC support was introduced in version 7.6, is currently experimental, and may not work for all projects. If you encounter any issues, contact us by opening a discussion on GitHub.\n\n## Get involved\n\nNow you're ready to use Next.js with Storybook. 🎉 If you use Nextjs at work, we'd love your feedback on the Next + Storybook experience.\n\nJoin the maintainers and our thriving community in Discord.\n\nTags\n\n🛠 CodeNextjsFramework\n\nContributors\n\n* ShaunEvening  \nShaunEvening\n\nJoin the community\n\nSubscribe\n\n7,044 developers and counting\n\nWhy\n\nWhy StorybookComponent driven UI\n\nDocs\n\nGuidesTutorialsChangelogTelemetry\n\nCommunity\n\nAddonsGet involvedBlog\n\nShowcase\n\nExploreProjectsComponent glossary\n\nOpen source software\n\nMaintained by\n\nChromatic\n\nSpecial thanks to Netlify and CircleCI",
      "title": "Integrate Next.js with Storybook | Storybook",

      "chunk": "skip to:contentpackage searchsign in\n\n❤\n\n* Pro\n* Teams\n* Pricing\n* Documentation\n\nnpm\n\nSearch\n\nSign UpSign In\n\n## @storybook/experimental-nextjs-vite\n\nTypeScript icon, indicating that this package has built-in type declarations\n\n8.6.14 • Public • Published 2 months ago\n\n* Readme\n* Code Beta\n* 6 Dependencies\n* 1 Dependents\n* 383 Versions\n\n# Storybook for Next.js with Vite Builder\n\nSee documentation for installation instructions, usage examples, APIs, and more.\n\n## Acknowledgements\n\nThis framework borrows heavily from these Storybook addons:\n\n* storybook-addon-next by RyanClementsHax\n* storybook-addon-next-router by lifeiscontent\n\n## Readme\n\n### Keywords\n\n* storybook\n* nextjs\n* vite\n\n## Package Sidebar\n\n### Install\n\n&#96;npm i @storybook/experimental-nextjs-vite&#96;\n\n### Repository\n\nGitgithub.com/storybookjs/storybook\n\n### Homepage\n\ngithub.com/storybookjs/storybook/tree/next/code/frameworks/experimental-nextjs-vite\n\n**Fund** this package\n\n### DownloadsWeekly Downloads\n\n93,853\n\n### Version\n\n8.6.14\n\n### License\n\nMIT\n\n### Unpacked Size\n\n236 kB\n\n### Total Files\n\n62\n\n### Last publish\n\n2 months ago\n\n### Collaborators\n\n* ndelangen\n* shilman\n* tmeasday\n* ghengeveld\n* winkervsbecks\n* yannbf\n* kylegach\n* jreinhold\n* kasperpeulen\n* valentinpalkovic\n* domyen\n* storybook-bot\n\n**Try** on RunKit\n\n**Report** malware\n\n## Footer\n\n### Support\n\n* Help\n* Advisories\n* Status\n* Contact npm\n\n### Company\n\n* About\n* Blog\n* Press\n\n### Terms \u0026 Policies\n\n* Policies\n* Terms of Use\n* Code of Conduct\n* Privacy",

      "chunk": "skip to:contentpackage searchsign in\n\n❤\n\n* Pro\n* Teams\n* Pricing\n* Documentation\n\nnpm\n\nSearch\n\nSign UpSign In\n\n## storybook-addon-next\n\n1.8.0 • Public • Published 2 years ago\n\n* Readme\n* Code Beta\n* 8 Dependencies\n* 8 Dependents\n* 30 Versions\n\n# Storybook Addon Next \n\n## ⚠️ DEPRECATED ⚠️ \n\nThis addon has been deprecated in favor of @storybook/nextjs which is the Storybook official addon for supporting Next.js features in Storybook. It supports everything &#96;storybook-addon-next&#96; does and much more! I even worked on developing this with them so you should be in good hands.\n\nConsult the migration docs for details on how to migrate.\n\n---\n\n**😱 No config support for Next.js**: Tired of writing and debugging webpack config? What Next.js supports out of the box, this addon makes possible in Storybook\n\ncurrent version Commitizen friendly semantic-release semantic-release: angular\n\n## Table of Contents \n\n* Supported Features\n* Requirements\n* Examples\n* Getting Started  \n   * Installation  \n   * Register the Addon in main.js  \n   * Partay\n* Documentation  \n   * Options  \n   * Next.js's Image Component (partial support)  \n         * Local Images  \n         * Remote Images  \n         * Optimization  \n         * AVIF  \n   * Next.js Routing  \n         * Overriding defaults  \n         * Global Defaults  \n         * Default Router  \n         * Actions Integration Caveats  \n   * Sass/Scss  \n   * Css/Sass/Scss Modules  \n   * Styled JSX  \n   * Postcss  \n   * Absolute Imports  \n   * Runtime Config  \n   * Custom Webpack Config  \n   * Typescript  \n   * next.config.js  \n         * ESM  \n   * Notes for Yarn v2 and v3 users  \n   * FAQ  \n         * Statically imported images won't load  \n         * This addon breaks when the .mjs extension for the next config is used  \n         * Module not found: Error: Can't resolve \\[package name\\]\n* Similar Projects\n* Want to suggest additional features?\n* Didn't find what you were looking for?\n\n## Supported Features\n\n👉 Next.js's Image Component (partial support)\n\n👉 Next.js Routing\n\n👉 Sass/Scss\n\n👉 Css/Sass/Scss Modules\n\n👉 Styled JSX\n\n👉 Postcss\n\n👉 Absolute Imports\n\n👉 Runtime Config\n\n👉 Custom Webpack Config\n\n👉 Typescript\n\n## Requirements\n\n* Next.js \\\u003e= 9.x\n* Storybook \\\u003e= 6.x  \n   * Storybook webpack 5 builder  \n         * Intro  \n         * Installation guide  \n         * It's not that this plugin can't support the webpack 4 builder, it's just that there hasn't been much of a need to and this is what Storybook recommends for nextjs apps. If you feel that you have a good use case, feel free to open up an issue.\n* Your Next.js config file uses the &#96;.js&#96; extension and not the &#96;.mjs&#96; extension (i.e. &#96;next.config.js&#96; not &#96;next.config.mjs&#96;)  \n   * See next.config.js for more details\n\n## Examples\n\n\u003e To run any example, first build the addon by running &#96;yarn build&#96; in the root of this repo.\n\n* Nextjs v13 - Source\n* Nextjs v12 - Source\n* Tailwindcss - Source\n* SVGR - Source\n* Nx - Source\n* Nextjs v11.1 - Source\n* Nextjs v11.0 - Source\n* Nextjs v10 - Source\n* Nextjs v9 - Source\n\n## Getting Started\n\n### Installation\n\nInstall &#96;storybook-addon-next&#96; using yarn:\n\nyarn add --dev storybook-addon-next\n\nOr npm:\n\nnpm install --save-dev storybook-addon-next\n\n### Register the Addon in main.js\n\n// .storybook/main.js\n\nmodule.exports = {\n  // other config ommited for brevity\n  addons: [\n    // ...\n    'storybook-addon-next'\n    // ...\n  ]\n}\n\n### Partay\n\n🥳🎉 Thats it! The supported features should work out of the box.\n\nSee Documentation for more details on how the supported features work in this addon.\n\nIf something doesn't work as you would expect, feel free to open up an issue.\n\n## Documentation\n\n### Options\n\nThis addon can be passed an options object for addional configuration if needed.\n\nFor example:\n\n// .storybook/main.js\nconst path = require('path')\n\nmodule.exports = {\n  // other config ommited for brevity\n  addons: [\n    // ...\n    {\n      name: 'storybook-addon-next',\n      options: {\n        nextConfigPath: path.resolve(__dirname, '../next.config.js')\n      }\n    }\n    // ...\n  ]\n}\n\n* &#96;nextConfigPath&#96;: The absolute path to the &#96;next.config.js&#96;\n\n### Next.js's Image Component (partial support)\n\nnext/image is notoriously difficult to get working with storybook. This addon allows you to use Next.js's &#96;Image&#96; component with no configuration!\n\n\u003e Because the image component has features, like image optimization, configured by options that require the Next.js config file to be read and processed by the framework and there is no public function exposed by Next.js to resolve and those options, it is not possible to support those features stably.\n\u003e \n\u003e If you want to see this better supported, feel free to contribute to the discussion on Next.js's side or the discussion on our side\n\n#### Local Images\n\nLocal images work just fine with this addon! Keep in mind that this feature was only added in Next.js v11.\n\nimport Image from 'next/image'\nimport profilePic from '../public/me.png'\n\nfunction Home() {\n  return (\n    \u003c\u003e\n      \u003ch1\u003eMy Homepage\u003c/h1\u003e\n      \u003cImage\n        src={profilePic}\n        alt=\"Picture of the author\"\n        // width={500} automatically provided\n        // height={500} automatically provided\n        // blurDataURL=\"../public/me.png\" set to equal the image itself (for this addon)\n        // placeholder=\"blur\" // Optional blur-up while loading\n      /\u003e\n      \u003cp\u003eWelcome to my homepage!\u003c/p\u003e\n    \u003c/\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n#### Remote Images\n\nRemote images also work just fine!\n\nimport Image from 'next/image'\n\nexport default function Home() {\n  return (\n    \u003c\u003e\n      \u003ch1\u003eMy Homepage\u003c/h1\u003e\n      \u003cImage\n        src=\"/me.png\"\n        alt=\"Picture of the author\"\n        width={500}\n        height={500}\n      /\u003e\n      \u003cp\u003eWelcome to my homepage!\u003c/p\u003e\n    \u003c/\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n#### Optimization\n\nAll Next.js &#96;Image&#96;s are automatically unoptimized for you.\n\nIf placeholder=\"blur\" is used, the blurDataURL used is the src of the image (thus effectively disabling the placeholder).\n\nSee this issue for more discussion on how Next.js &#96;Image&#96;s are handled for Storybook.\n\n#### AVIF\n\nThis format is not supported by this addon yet. Feel free to open up an issue if this is something you want to see.\n\n### Next.js Routing\n\nThis solution is heavily based on storybook-addon-next-router so a big thanks to &#96;lifeiscontent&#96; for providing a good solution that this addon could work off of.\n\nNext.js's router is automatically stubbed for you so that when the router is interacted with, all of its interactions are automatically logged to the Storybook actions tab if you have the actions addon.\n\n#### Overriding defaults\n\nPer-story overrides can be done by adding a &#96;nextRouter&#96; property onto the story parameters. The addon will shallowly merge whatever you put here into the router.\n\nimport SomeComponentThatUsesTheRouter from \"./SomeComponentThatUsesTheRouter\";\n\nexport default {\n  title: \"My Story\",\n};\n\n// if you have the actions addon\n// you can click the links and see the route change events there\nexport const Example = () =\u003e \u003cSomeComponentThatUsesTheRouter /\u003e;\n\nExample.parameters: {\n  nextRouter: {\n    path: \"/profile/[id]\",\n    asPath: \"/profile/ryanclementshax\",\n    query: {\n      id: \"ryanclementshax\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nSee this example for a reference.\n\n#### Global Defaults\n\nGlobal defaults can be set in preview.js and will be shallowly merged with the default router.\n\nexport const parameters = {\n  nextRouter: {\n    path: '/some-default-path',\n    asPath: '/some-default-path',\n    query: {}\n  }\n}\n\nSee this example for a reference.\n\n#### Default Router\n\nThe default values on the stubbed router are as follows (see globals for more details on how globals work)\n\nconst defaultRouter = {\n  locale: context?.globals?.locale,\n  route: '/',\n  pathname: '/',\n  query: {},\n  asPath: '/',\n  push(...args: unknown[]) {\n    action('nextRouter.push')(...args)\n    return Promise.resolve(true)\n  },\n  replace(...args: unknown[]) {\n    action('nextRouter.replace')(...args)\n    return Promise.resolve(true)\n  },\n  reload(...args: unknown[]) {\n    action('nextRouter.reload')(...args)\n  },\n  back(...args: unknown[]) {\n    action('nextRouter.back')(...args)\n  },\n  prefetch(...args: unknown[]) {\n    action('nextRouter.prefetch')(...args)\n    return Promise.resolve()\n  },\n  beforePopState(...args: unknown[]) {\n    action('nextRouter.beforePopState')(...args)\n  },\n  events: {\n    on(...args: unknown[]) {\n      action('nextRouter.events.on')(...args)\n    },\n    off(...args: unknown[]) {\n      action('nextRouter.events.off')(...args)\n    },\n    emit(...args: unknown[]) {\n      action('nextRouter.events.emit')(...args)\n    }\n  },\n  isFallback: false\n}\n\n#### Actions Integration Caveats\n\nIf you override a function, you lose the automatic action tab integration and have to build it out yourself.\n\nexport const parameters = {\n  nextRouter: {\n    push() {\n      // we lose the default implementation that logs the action into the action tab\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nDoing this yourself looks something like this (make sure you install the &#96;@storybook/addon-actions&#96; package):\n\nimport { action } from '@storybook/addon-actions'\n\nexport const parameters = {\n  nextRouter: {\n    push(...args) {\n      // custom logic can go here\n      // this logs to the actions tab\n      action('nextRouter.push')(...args)\n      // return whatever you want here\n      return Promise.resolve(true)\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n### Sass/Scss\n\nGlobal sass/scss stylesheets are supported without any additional configuration as well. Just import them into preview.js\n\nimport '../styles/globals.scss'\n\nThis will automatically include any of your custom sass configurations in your &#96;next.config.js&#96; file.\n\n\u003e Right now only the &#96;.js&#96; extension of the Next.js config is supported, not &#96;.mjs&#96;. See next.config.js for more details.\n\nconst path = require('path')\n\nmodule.exports = {\n  // any options here are included in sass compilation for your stories\n  sassOptions: {\n    includePaths: [path.join(__dirname, 'styles')]\n  }\n}\n\n### Css/Sass/Scss Modules\n\nNext.js supports css modules out of the box so this addon supports it too.\n\n// this import works just fine in Storybook now\nimport styles from './Button.module.css'\n// sass/scss is also supported\n// import styles from './Button.module.scss'\n// import styles from './Button.module.sass'\n\nexport function Button() {\n  return (\n    \u003cbutton type=\"button\" className={styles.error}\u003e\n      Destroy\n    \u003c/button\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n### Styled JSX\n\nThe built in CSS in JS solution for Next.js is styled-jsx, and this addon supports that out of the box too, zero config.\n\n// This works just fine in Storybook with this addon\nfunction HelloWorld() {\n  return (\n    \u003cdiv\u003e\n      Hello world\n      \u003cp\u003escoped!\u003c/p\u003e\n      \u003cstyle jsx\u003e{&#96;\n        p {\n          color: blue;\n        }\n        div {\n          background: red;\n        }\n        @media (max-width: 600px) {\n          div {\n            background: blue;\n          }\n        }\n      &#96;}\u003c/style\u003e\n      \u003cstyle global jsx\u003e{&#96;\n        body {\n          background: black;\n        }\n      &#96;}\u003c/style\u003e\n    \u003c/div\u003e\n  )\n}\n\nexport default HelloWorld\n\nYou can use your own babel config too. This is an example of how you can customize styled-jsx.\n\n// .babelrc or whatever config file you use\n{\n  \"presets\": [\n    [\n      \"next/babel\",\n      {\n        \"styled-jsx\": {\n          \"plugins\": [\"@styled-jsx/plugin-sass\"]\n        }\n      }\n    ]\n  ]\n}\n\nIf you use a monorepo, you may need to add the babel config yourself to your storybook project. Just add a babel config to your storybook project with the following contents to get started.\n\n{\n  \"presets\": [\"next/babel\"]\n}\n\n### Postcss\n\nNext.js lets you customize postcss config. Thus this addon will automatically handle your postcss config for you.\n\nThis allows for cool things like zero config tailwindcss! See the with-tailwindcss example for reference! Its a clone of Next.js's tailwindcss example set up with storybook and this addon.\n\n### Absolute Imports\n\nGoodbye &#96;../&#96;! Absolute imports from the root directory work just fine with this addon.\n\n// All good!\nimport Button from 'components/button'\n// Also good!\nimport styles from 'styles/HomePage.module.css'\n\nexport default function HomePage() {\n  return (\n    \u003c\u003e\n      \u003ch1 className={styles.title}\u003eHello World\u003c/h1\u003e\n      \u003cButton /\u003e\n    \u003c/\u003e\n  )\n}\n\n// preview.js\n\n// Also ok in preview.js!\nimport 'styles/globals.scss'\n\n// ...\n\n### Runtime Config\n\nNext.js allows for Runtime Configuration which lets you import a handy &#96;getConfig&#96; function to get certain configuration defined in your &#96;next.config.js&#96; file at runtime.\n\nIn the context of Storybook with this addon, you can expect Next.js's Runtime Configuration feature to work just fine.\n\nNote, because Storybook doesn't server render your components, your components will only see what they normally see on the client side (i.e. they won't see &#96;serverRuntimeConfig&#96; but will see &#96;publicRuntimeConfig&#96;).\n\nFor example, consider the following Next.js config:\n\n// next.config.js\nmodule.exports = {\n  serverRuntimeConfig: {\n    mySecret: 'secret',\n    secondSecret: process.env.SECOND_SECRET // Pass through env variables\n  },\n  publicRuntimeConfig: {\n    staticFolder: '/static'\n  }\n}\n\nCalls to &#96;getConfig&#96; would return the following object when called within Storybook:\n\n{\n  \"serverRuntimeConfig\": {},\n  \"publicRuntimeConfig\": {\n    \"staticFolder\": \"/static\"\n  }\n}\n\n### Custom Webpack Config\n\nNext.js comes with a lot of things for free out of the box like sass support, but sometimes we add custom webpack config modifications to Next.js. This addon takes care of most of the webpack modifications you would want to add. If Next.js supports a feature out of the box, then this addon will make that feature work out of the box in Storybook. If Next.js doesn't support something out of the box, but makes it easy to configure, then this addon will do the same for that thing for Storybook. If you find something that you still need to configure webpack to get a Next.js feature to work in Storybook after adding this addon, this is likely a bug and please feel free to open up an issue.\n\nAny webpack modifications desired for Storybook should be made in .storybook/main.js according to Storybook's docs.\n\nNote: Not all webpack modifications are copy/paste-able between &#96;next.config.js&#96; and &#96;.storybook/main.js&#96;. It is recommended to do your reasearch on how to properly make your modifcation to Storybook's webpack config and on how webpack works.\n\nPlease feel free to contribute an example to help out the community.\n\nBelow is an example of how to add svgr support to Storybook with this addon. The full example can be found here.\n\n// .storybook/main.js\nmodule.exports = {\n  // other config omitted for brevity\n  webpackFinal: async config =\u003e {\n    // this modifies the existing image rule to exclude .svg files\n    // since we want to handle those files with @svgr/webpack\n    const imageRule = config.module.rules.find(rule =\u003e rule.test.test('.svg'))\n    imageRule.exclude = /\\.svg$/\n\n    // configure .svg files to be loaded with @svgr/webpack\n    config.module.rules.push({\n      test: /\\.svg$/,\n      use: ['@svgr/webpack']\n    })\n\n    return config\n  }\n}\n\n### Typescript\n\nStorybook handles most Typescript configurations, but this addon adds additional support for Next.js's support for Absolute Imports and Module path aliases. In short, it takes into account your &#96;tsconfig.json&#96;'s baseUrl and paths. Thus, a &#96;tsconfig.json&#96; like the one below would work out of the box.\n\n{\n  \"compilerOptions\": {\n    \"baseUrl\": \".\",\n    \"paths\": {\n      \"@/components/*\": [\"components/*\"]\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n### next.config.js\n\n#### ESM\n\nRight now the only supported config format for Next.js that this plugin supports is the commonjs version of the config (i.e. &#96;next.config.js&#96;). This is mostly because I haven't figured out how to require a &#96;.mjs&#96; file from a storybook addon (which is bound to commonjs modules as far as I know right now). If you are able to help, I'd love it if you could contribute to this discussion to get support for the &#96;.mjs&#96; version if such support is even possible.\n\n### Notes for Yarn v2 and v3 users\n\nIf you're using Yarn v2 or v3, you may run into issues where Storybook can't resolve &#96;style-loader&#96; or &#96;css-loader&#96;. For example, you might get errors like:\n\n&#96;Module not found: Error: Can't resolve 'css-loader'&#96;  \n&#96;Module not found: Error: Can't resolve 'style-loader'&#96;\n\nThis is because those versions of Yarn have different package resolution rules than Yarn v1.x. If this is the case for you, just install the package directly.\n\n### FAQ\n\n#### Statically imported images won't load\n\nMake sure you are treating image imports the same way you treat them when using next image in normal development.\n\nBefore &#96;storybook-addon-next&#96;, image imports just imported the raw path to the image (e.g. &#96;'static/media/stories/assets/plugin.svg'&#96;). When using &#96;storybook-addon-next&#96; image imports work the \"Next.js way\" meaning that we now get an object when we import an image. For example:\n\n{\n  \"src\": \"static/media/stories/assets/plugin.svg\",\n  \"height\": 48,\n  \"width\": 48,\n  \"blurDataURL\": \"static/media/stories/assets/plugin.svg\"\n}\n\nTherefore, if something in storybook isn't showing the image properly, make sure you expect the object to be returned from an import instead of just the asset path.\n\nSee local images for more detail on how Next.js treats static image imports.\n\n#### This addon breaks when the .mjs extension for the next config is used\n\nRight now using &#96;next.config.mjs&#96; isn't supported by this addon. See next.config.js for more details. Right now, it is required for you to use the &#96;.js&#96; extension instead. Feel free to help out on this discussion to get this supported.\n\n#### Module not found: Error: Can't resolve \\[package name\\]\n\nYou might get this if you're using Yarn v2 or v3\\. See Notes for Yarn v2 and v3 users for more details.\n\n## Similar Projects\n\n* storybook-addon-next-router\n\n## Want to suggest additional features?\n\nI'm open to discussion. Feel free to open up an issue.\n\n## Didn't find what you were looking for?\n\nWas this documentation insufficient for you?\n\nWas it confusing?\n\nWas it ... dare I say ... inaccurate?\n\nIf any of the above describes your feelings of this documentation. Feel free to open up an issue.\n\n## Readme\n\n### Keywords\n\n* storybook\n* addon\n* next\n* nextjs\n\n## Package Sidebar\n\n### Install\n\n&#96;npm i storybook-addon-next&#96;\n\n### Repository\n\nGitgithub.com/RyanClementsHax/storybook-addon-next\n\n### Homepage\n\ngithub.com/RyanClementsHax/storybook-addon-next#readme\n\n### DownloadsWeekly Downloads\n\n21,051\n\n### Version\n\n1.8.0\n\n### License\n\nMIT\n\n### Unpacked Size\n\n51 kB\n\n### Total Files\n\n21\n\n### Last publish\n\n2 years ago\n\n### Collaborators\n\n* ryanclementshax\n\n**Try** on RunKit\n\n**Report** malware\n\n## Footer\n\n### Support\n\n* Help\n* Advisories\n* Status\n* Contact npm\n\n### Company\n\n* About\n* Blog\n* Press\n\n### Terms \u0026 Policies\n\n* Policies\n* Terms of Use\n* Code of Conduct\n* Privacy",
